native_boundary: Existing optional shared application-command filter from Libraries/NativeUI/command-filter-source-audit.json. Native NSMenu/NSTextView own controls, shortcut interpretation, validation dispatch and action dispatch.

bindings.views: Call actual OmniboxViewViews IsTextEditCommandEnabled and ExecuteTextEditCommand, retaining its asynchronous paste, rejection policy and URL sanitization.
bindings.blink: Call actual ClipboardCommands EnabledCopy/Cut/Paste with MenuOrKeyBinding source 0. Execute actual EditorCommand with the original KeyboardEvent. Browser handlers retain trusted events, cancellation, clipboard data and undo.

findings: A browser-owned Wayland clipboard can contain text while the offscreen helper NSPasteboard has no types. Native post-action reporting cannot enable Paste in that state.

One dispatcher chooses the active Views or Blink transaction so each process does not replace its own command handler with a different binding. Process, control, field and live-frame identity are checked before execution.

A claimed application action suppresses native mutation. Once an application action was attempted, Views reports the key handled even if the helper response or field disappears, preventing a second original action.

No native control, clipboard algorithm, menu implementation or shortcut table is copied. NativeUI provider, loader, shim, Chromium and installed AppKit are unchanged. Only the small Chromium adapter is rebuilt.
